cite: Edgar A. Levy Leasing Co. v. Siegel, 194 A.D. 482
court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: The court sustained as a valid exercise of the police power the 1920 emergency rent statutes limiting landlords in New York City to reasonable rents during the postwar housing shortage, while the statutory scheme it construed separately carved out and specially regulated hotels and short-term lodging/rooming-house lettings.

quotes.text: but hotels, lodging and rooming houses are excepted therefrom.
agreed to a renewal of the lease for the further period of two years from October 1, 1920
It follows that the order should be affirmed, with ten dollars costs and disbursements.

notes: Primarily an ordinary long-term apartment lease dispute, but the opinion extensively discusses police-power regulation of the letting business (analogized to innkeeping/warehousing) and the statutes' explicit carve-outs for hotels and week-or-less lodging/rooming-house lettings, so it bears on regulation of short-term letting even though not squarely on point.
